key_insight: KQML-Liver combines quantum machine learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, reporting 82% accuracy and 100% recall for liver disease classification.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support interpretable liver disease screening, but its clinical usefulness remains unproven.
method: Parameterized quantum circuits represent input features.
Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks model nonlinear relationships through interpretable functional mappings.
Preprocessing is designed to prevent data leakage.
evidence_signal: On the Indian Liver Patient Dataset, the authors report 82% accuracy and detection of all positive cases under a leakage-prevention protocol.
watch_item: The abstract reports no external validation or specificity, leaving generalizability and false-positive burden unclear.
paper_title: KQML-Liver: Interpretable Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Liver Disease Classification
